visualDebt: Polyps carry six tentacle tubes instead of the twelve of a real Acropora polyp (LOD1 triangle budget).

Only the prominent radial corallites are modelled (up to eleven per branch, some dropped where a neighbouring branch is too close); the dense field of small radials is carried by the texture relief and roughness.
Corallites are flared tubes with a recessed calice; the nariform (longer lower lip) profile and the septa are texture only.
The tabular plate is a lobed, radially ridged solid lens rather than a perforated mesh of anastomosing horizontal branchlets.
Retraction folds the tentacles to about half length (0.3 of the length on the hairy form) rather than fully into the calice.

Polyp crowns are one rigid unskinned mesh per branch cluster with morph targets rather than skinned geometry; this works around a glTF importer and runtime-gate interaction, see the lane shared-change-request. Per-polyp variation comes from seeded tentacle geometry, per-polyp flutter directions and two interleaved flutter halves per cluster, not from independent per-polyp phases.
The hairy form is the digitate layout with short thick branchlets; A. millepora's plate-like fused base and the coenosteum spinules are texture only.
Polyps carry six tentacle tubes instead of the twelve of a real acroporid polyp (LOD1 triangle budget).
Only about one corallite in three carries a modelled polyp; the remaining corallites are painted pits with a raised lower lip in the branch texture.
Loose anastomosis (branches fusing where they touch) is not modelled; every branch is a separate closed tube kept clear of its neighbours.

Polyps of one branch share one cluster bone: lean, swirl and pulsing are uniform along the branch apart from a bend gradient toward the tip and per-polyp skin gain; retraction pulls polyps toward the branch axis, so on curved branches the retracted depth varies slightly along the branch.
The reticulate coenosteum and corallite septa are texture relief only.

Modelled polyps are the prominent fraction of the real dense field (about one nub per 3 mm of tissue); the remaining corallites and their tiny polyps are suggested by the painted calices, hoods and polyp speckle.

Each polyp is a four sided nub with a slightly flared crown and recessed mouth; the six short tentacles of a real Stylophora polyp are painted as crown grooves, not modelled, so polyps read as small pale blocks at close range.
Polyps are shown extended; in the wild Stylophora pistillata extends its polyps mainly at night (WoRMS description), the aquarium blueberry morph is commonly seen with polyps out by day.
Retraction pulls each crown toward its branch axis, so polyps on the rounded knob within about 40 degrees of the apex only partially retract and slide slightly toward the branch axis.
Fork blades are elliptical tube sections; the flattened, slightly spatulate tips of some wild colonies are not modelled.
The mound apex cap keeps the polar fan UV of the dome loft, so its tissue texture streaks radially at the very top (mostly hidden under the central leader).
The pink seed keeps three primaries unforked because the compact layout leaves less than the 2.2 mm minimum branch gap for their forks; the blueberry seed forks all primaries but one.
Skeleton is static by design (user rule for stony corals): no branch flex in any clip.

visualDebt: Polyp retraction is a partial contraction (stalks shorten to roughly 60 percent and deflate 22 percent radially); polyps do not vanish fully into their calices.

Tentacles gather toward the oral axis through the head's radial deflation only; the authored fold shape key is not baked because the pinned glTF importer renames animated skinned meshes and the runtime parity gate rejects that.
Corallite calices and septa are painted (albedo/normal) rather than modelled as recessed cups.
Tentacles are 3-segment tubes with a single shared bone per polyp; no per-tentacle motion.

Dactylozooids are drawn about twice their real diameter (0.28 mm radius) and at a fraction of their real density so they read at LOD1; real colonies carry thousands of finer hairs per square centimetre.
Gastropores and dactylopores are painted as cyclosystem speckle in the albedo and normal maps, not modelled as holes.

Hairs in one cluster share a bone: bending comes from root-to-tip weight blending plus baked per-hair lean and gain, so hairs within a cluster move in step with a small twist gradient; hair-vs-hair clearance is not proven.

Branching form: dichotomous forks are fused intersecting tubes (parent knuckle plus two children) rather than a single smoothed junction; sibling branches are not clearance-checked against each other at the fork.
Blade form: blades are separate lofts that root in the encrusting base and do not fuse into the honeycomb plates seen in M. platyphylla.

candidates.displayName: Montipora capricornis (orange whorling plate, green polyps)

variants.displayName: Montipora capricornis (orange whorling plate, green polyps)

visualDebt: Polyp density is far below reality (220 to 270 modelled polyps per colony versus thousands of 0.5 to 1.5 mm corallites); the remaining corallites are painted as pits in the tissue textures.
Each polyp is a six-sided tube with a flared crown; the twelve tentacles of a real Montipora polyp are painted on the crown, not modelled.

Polyp tubes are 1.8 to 2.6 mm in design space and scale with the colony normalisation (the digitata variant lands at 2.2 to 3.1 mm, 1.7 to 2.6 mm exposed), slightly above the 1 to 2 mm of live polyps.

Tuberculae are modelled on the encrusting sheet only and its polyps keep to slopes under 17 degrees (tubercle flanks carry painted corallites only); on the plate and fingers tuberculae are normal-map relief.

Retraction translates polyps along their cluster axis into the corallite (tips stop about 0.5 mm above the surface) instead of morphing tissue over them; finger polyps between the four sector directions retract to 70 to 100 percent of the pull.
The whorling plate is one continuous 2.6-turn scroll; real M. capricornis colonies often stack several separate tiers and fuse plates.
Finger forks stay fused to their parent for part of their length (anastomosing habit) and carry polyps only on their free side.
Tentacle acrospheres are lofted knobs on a six-sided tube; at close range the knob silhouette is faceted.
Septa inside the calice are not modelled; the oral disc covers the calice so only the outer costae relief (normal map) reads.

Tentacles of one cluster share a three-bone chain (two clusters per head within the 32-bone budget); bending along each tentacle comes from arc-length skinning to that shared chain plus baked per-tentacle lean, sag and curl, not from a chain per tentacle.
Retraction is driven by chain scale and curl toward the disc axis, so retracted tentacles fold into a tuft rather than deflating into wrinkled nubs.
Tentacles of one polyp may overlap tentacles of a neighbouring polyp (as in live colonies); only tentacle-vs-skeleton and tentacle-vs-disc clearances are proven.
Tentacle fringe is modelled with 20 to 24 tapered tubes per polyp; real Zoanthus carry 40 to 60 shorter tentacles in two or three cycles.
Coenenchyme mat is a raised plateau and per-polyp collar relief on the rock loft rather than a separate tissue layer with stolons.
Closing is a single staggered pulse per cluster; real polyps close in seconds and reopen over minutes.
Polyps are bone-parented rigid objects that sway about their base; the column itself does not bend (this keeps shape-key clips importable, see the lane's shared-change request).

Neighbouring discs stop short of touching by the flattest tentacle reach plus a sway margin, because the clearance gates forbid tentacle and disc interpenetration; real mats overlap discs and interleave fringes.
Arms are straight tubes; live animals often show slight lateral arm curvature and per-individual length asymmetry beyond the mild front/side/rear variation modelled here.
Granules are a normal-map relief only; no modelled plate geometry.
Ambulacral groove is a shallow cross-section dip with painted tube feet; no individual tube-foot geometry.
Disc and arm bases are overlapping closed solids; the interradial crotch is an intersection crease rather than a blended surface.
Hub dome is about 4.6 cm across interradially, slightly larger than the 3-4 cm disc Laxton (1974) measured, because it must cover the five arm-tube junctions.
Pleopods are single paddles per segment rather than biramous rami with setae.
Antennular flagella are two smooth tubes per side; the real outer flagellum forks with a setose thickened portion.
Rostral teeth and carapace spines are implied by the normal map, not modelled.
Legs use a single bone each except the chelipeds, so knees do not articulate while walking.
Orbital hoods are smooth ellipsoids fused to the carapace rather than a sculpted anterior margin.
The major palm's dorsal saddle notch is only hinted by the loft profile and texture.
Setae and leg bristles are texture-only; pleopods do not beat.

Major chela proportions follow general Alpheus descriptions, not A. bellulus specific measurements; the rest pose includes the forward-held chela in the 50 mm x extent (rostrum to telson about 41 mm).
Epipodial tentacles along the foot margin and the calcareous operculum are not modelled.
Axial folds are geometric knobs on the loft; the two impressed spiral lines, growth striae and basal lirae are normal-map relief only.
Shell colour is the aquarium olive-tan morph with algal film; the reddish-orange wild morph of Lithopoma tectum is not offered as a variant.
Whorl interior near the columella is a self-overlapping tube rather than a true shared-wall shell.
Aperture is the constricted, obliquely sheared end of the whorl tube; the thickened columellar callus and bidentate columella are not modelled.
The body column that fills the aperture is a smooth lofted mass without a distinct mantle edge, and the eyes are simple beads on short stalks.

rows.scientificLabel: Ophiuroidea (reef brittle star, Ophiocoma / Ophioderma group)
visualDebt: Lateral spines are one or two spikes per plate side; Ophiocoma echinata carries a vertical row of four graded spines per side of each arm joint.
Ventral disc (jaws, oral shields, bursal slits) and the pale oral arm surface are texture-only because the animal rests on them.
Arm segmentation is 26 plates per arm for the triangle budget; real arms carry many more, shorter vertebrae.
Rest pose is mirror symmetric (leading arm straight in plan) so the shared bilateral gates apply; live animals hold every arm in a different curve.
Spiral cords and beads are geometric only on the last five whorls; earlier whorls carry the sculpture in the normal map alone.

Whorls are a single swept tube that overlaps itself to form sutures, with a thin columella plug closing the axis; the shell wall has no modelled thickness and the aperture interior is a shallow recessed cap behind the neck.
The operculum is not modelled and the aperture is nearly circular rather than the slightly oblique oval of real Cerithium.
The rounded shell base reads dark in the front orthographic view; base flecking and lighting could be improved.
Soft-part proportions (foot, snout, siphon) are inferred from general cerithiid anatomy rather than calibrated live photographs, and the tentacles are straight tapered tubes without curl.
Leg and cheliped setae (hair) are painted flecks in the albedo/roughness/normal maps, not modelled fibres.
Mouthparts (maxillipeds) and antennules are not modelled; the frontal region is the carapace margin plus eyestalks and antennae.
Carapace sculpture is a smooth lobe displacement plus a granular normal map rather than individually modelled tubercles.
Sideways walk is a kinematic loop with the body fixed in place; the runtime must translate the root along the crab's lateral axis to sell the gait.
Shell is one self-overlapping closed loft: whorls overlap inside the shell as in life, but the union surface is not resolved, so the suture is a geometric step rather than a modelled channel.
Shoulder knobs are ring displacements at 64 rings per whorl, so they read as blunt scallops rather than sculpted nodules; the 36-segment rings show mild faceting on the ramp.
Operculum serrations and the mantle edge are not modelled; the sickle operculum is a smooth flattened tube.
Eye pattern is a texture on an ellipsoid (no separate cornea); eyestalks retract by bone scaling, which also shrinks the eye.

Eyestalk versus shell clearance is not declared: during withdraw the retracting stalks pass the parietal wall inside the aperture region. Eyestalks are proven clear of the foot, the proboscis and each other in every clip.
Shell colour is procedural mottling with flammules and spiral bands, not a calibrated pattern from a specific specimen.
Aperture interior (columella, parietal callus, lip teeth) is a capped loft filled by the soft body column rather than modelled shell interior.
Beaded sculpture is a smooth radius relief plus normal map; individual beads are not separate nodules.
Operculum is not modelled (hidden under the shell while crawling).
Abdomen and pleopods are not modelled (hidden inside the shell); the body ends as a capped loft inside the aperture.
Third maxillipeds and other mouthparts are absent; the anterior shield margin is rounded without a modelled rostrum or frontal teeth.
Each limb is one pinched tube per appendage, so articulations flex as skin rather than as true condylar joints; no setae or tubercles are modelled (granules are texture-only).

The borrowed shell is a generic authored turbinate form with a recessed aperture floor; no columella, inner lip or specific gastropod species is represented. It is carried low with the lower body whorl about half a millimetre above the substrate rather than touching it, and the walk clip rocks and surges it in place (clips do not translate along the ground).

The dextral carry has the spire pointing back, slightly up and to the crab's right rather than straight back: with the aperture facing forward-down, a straight-back spire would force the coil axis level with the ground or lifted.
The left chela is only 8 percent larger than the right; both chelae are smooth tubes without the tuberculate palm surface.

The shell is a strictly self-similar conispiral, so its base is a shallow spiral ramp (lowest at the aperture lip); the body hump fills most of the space under it but the front whorl still overhangs the mantle edge.
Beaded spiral cords, growth striae and the suture are normal-map relief only; the shell geometry itself is smooth.
No operculum, mouth or epipodial skirt is modelled; epipodial tentacles attach directly to the foot flank and the eyes are stalkless black ellipsoids.
Soft-body proportions in life position are inferred from general trochid anatomy (reference grade B for the shell, weaker for the animal).
Successive whorls are a single self-overlapping lofted tube: the suture reads as an intersection crease rather than a modelled overlap seam.
Aperture is capped with a flat nacre disc behind the neck instead of a modelled columella and interior.
Spiral cord beading and fine lirulae are normal-map relief only; the mesh carries just the shoulder nodules and the broad cord undulation.

Retract draws the shrinking tentacles back under the lip into the body whorl, so shell-vs-tentacle clearance is asserted implicitly by geometry in rest and crawl (about 7 mm and 10 mm) but not as a validator constraint.
